heading: EXT. HIGH DESERT - LONE CABIN - MORNING

units.text: EXT. HIGH DESERT - LONE CABIN - MORNING
A silver wind combs the sage.
ELIJAH FARROW, 50s, sits on the porch step in a sun-faded hat, a tin cup steaming in his hands.

His horse dozes at the post, tail flicking, while a crow on the fence rail considers him with one black eye, the wind rattles a loose shutter, the dog's shadow slides across the dust, and Elijah sips, tips back his hat, and waits for something he doesn't name.
Dear Ruth. The roof held through the storm.
units.name: ELIJAH

units.text: A rider, small, grows on the horizon.
I expect I'll have company soon. Don't worry. I've kept the kettle on.
units.name: ELIJAH

units.text: The rider comes closer, and the crow lifts off the rail.
Elijah stands slowly, wipes his hands on his trousers, and walks inside.
He lifts the shotgun from its pegs above the door and breaks it open.
He closes the gun with a soft, sure click.
